body: High: a non-empty operator-writable worktree value exempts an entity from completion gating and can permit an away-status mutation without a committed Stage Report.
High: merge guard --verdict passed can arm or clear a merge mod-block before the later incomplete-report transition refusal.
High: non-Git, untracked, ignored, or unborn-HEAD entity state cannot satisfy the committed path-clean completion predicate.
Medium: an older committed report can satisfy a later entry into the same stage because no stage-entry generation is persisted.
Low: per-candidate report durability checks spawn Git subprocesses on status --next and boot hot paths.
Low: merge proof permits only mod-block and pr frontmatter deltas, so other uncommitted fields can produce a completion refusal.
Low: gate and terminal exclusions are suppressed earlier in dispatch analysis and their runSet necessity lacks a focused mutation assertion.
Low: the CLI merge test seeds one hardcoded entity report and may surprise future sibling-entity tests.

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: accepted AC-4 explicitly leaves worktree-marked in-flight entities to existing worktree and roster suppression, so the normal released FO workflow loses no accepted outcome and the cited trigger is a manual mutation sequence; promotes-when: a supported FO trace advances a worktree-marked entered stage without its retained completion review

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: the released FO invokes passed merge finalization only after completion review, while the cited out-of-order direct invocation cannot advance status and breaks no accepted value criterion; promotes-when: a supported FO journey invokes passed merge guard before the committed report or the early mod-block mutation causes observable workflow loss

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: accepted AC-3 requires path-clean committed recovery evidence and the documented split-root workflow uses a versioned checkout, so Git-less or unborn state is outside the promised recovery workflow and no supported user loses an accepted outcome; promotes-when: the public workflow contract promises entered-stage recovery for non-versioned entity state

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: accepted AC-4 explicitly defers same-stage re-entry identity because current gate topology and feedback routing do not reach that scheduler path, so no normal released workflow can trigger the loss; promotes-when: a gate can target a previously visited stage or feedback recovery begins using status --next

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: these are scaling, diagnostic, and fixture-maintainability observations with no current user-visible loss or accepted safety boundary at risk in the supported workflow; promotes-when: measured active-set latency regresses or a sanctioned pre-merge mutation or fixture false-green causes an observable supported-workflow failure
